_about: Poll closing times for the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. Daylight saving time ends Nov. 1, so Eastern is EST (UTC-5) on Election Day. 'close' = when the last polls in the state close (UTC); 'first' = when polls close in the state's earlier time zone, if different. 'early_districts' lists House districts lying entirely in the earlier time zone; every other district in a split state uses 'close'.

AK.note: Most of Alaska closes at 8 PM Alaska time (midnight ET), when networks treat the state as callable; the western Aleutians close an hour later. Ranked-choice tabulation, if needed, comes weeks later.

FL.note: The western panhandle is on Central time and closes an hour after the rest of Florida.

GA.note: A candidate needs 50% to avoid a runoff.

ID.note: The northern panhandle is on Pacific time and closes an hour after southern Idaho.

IN.note: Counties near Chicago and Evansville are on Central time.

KS.note: Four western counties are on Mountain time.

KY.note: Western Kentucky is on Central time; networks often treat the state as mostly closed at 6 PM ET.

LA.note: House races are an all-candidate primary on Nov. 3, with Dec. 12 runoffs where no one tops 50%.

ME.note: Federal races use ranked-choice voting if no one wins a majority.

MI.note: Four Upper Peninsula counties are on Central time.

NE.note: Polls close at the same moment in both time zones.

ND.note: Most polling places close earlier; the latest close at 9 PM local time in each time zone.

OR.note: Vote-by-mail; ballots are due at 8 PM local time. Malheur County is on Mountain time.

SD.note: West River is on Mountain time.

TN.note: Polls close at the same moment in both time zones.

TX.note: Only El Paso and Hudspeth counties are on Mountain time.

WA.note: Vote-by-mail; ballots are due at 8 PM local time.
